source.title_on_document: How AI Ideas Affect the Creativity, Diversity, and Evolution of Human Ideas: Evidence From a Large, Dynamic Experiment

paper_design_summary: Online volunteers (844 unique participants from Reddit, Facebook ads, and the Creative Mornings newsletter) each completed up to five Alternate Uses Task trials. Before each trial they ranked six example ideas, and the share of ChatGPT-3.5 ideas among the examples (0, 2, or 4) and whether AI ideas were labeled were varied across five conditions, with each person randomized to a sequence that visits each condition once with a different item. Human examples came from prior participants in the same condition (dynamic response chains); the submitted ideas were scored for originality by a fine-tuned GPT-3 classifier and for diversity with SBERT embeddings.

studies.label: Dynamic online AUT experiment (AI exposure x disclosure)

assignment.what_was_assigned: A sequence of five (condition, item) trials. Each of the five conditions (Control: 0 AI + 6 human examples; Low exposure: 2 AI + 4 human; High exposure: 4 AI + 2 human; each exposure level with AI ideas labeled or unlabeled) is mapped to one of five AUT items so that neither conditions nor items repeat within a person's sequence.
assignment.quote: Participants are randomized to a sequence of 5 trials. In each trial, participants generate a creative use for an item under a specific experimental condition. Neither items nor conditions repeat in a 5-trial sequence.
assignment.locator: p. 5, Figure 2 caption and Section 3.4.2 (Randomization); conditions in p. 2, Figure 1

arms.name: Control
arms.description: Six human example ideas (most recent ideas from prior participants in the same condition-item chain, seeded from the Organisciak dataset); no AI ideas; disclosure = No

arms.name: Low Exposure, Undisclosed
arms.description: 2 ChatGPT ideas + 4 human ideas; AI ideas not labeled

arms.name: Low Exposure, Disclosed
arms.description: 2 ChatGPT ideas + 4 human ideas; AI ideas labeled as AI

arms.name: High Exposure, Undisclosed
arms.description: 4 ChatGPT ideas + 2 human ideas; AI ideas not labeled

arms.name: High Exposure, Disclosed
arms.description: 4 ChatGPT ideas + 2 human ideas; AI ideas labeled as AI

participants.exclusions: Only participants who completed at least one trial are analyzed (number who consented but completed none is not given). 2 responses that should not have been shown and 36 profane responses were removed: 3,414 responses analyzed of 3,452 (SI 3, pp. 17-18). Average 4.05 responses per participant (Table 2). The regression models for creativity and local diversity report 3,271 observations (Tables 14, 18); the gap from 3,414 is not explained.
participants.who: Unpaid adult volunteers (verified 18+) recruited through the Creative Mornings newsletter (343, 40.6%), r/InternetIsBeautiful (298, 35.3%), r/samplesize (94), shared links (61), other subreddits and Facebook ads; the paper describes them as technology-interested users and creative professionals. Mean age 34.92 (SD 10.86).
participants.country: 48 countries; top five by responses (77.85% of responses): United States, Canada, Germany, United Kingdom, Australia
participants.quote: Unique Participants 844; Total Responses 3414; Avg Responses/Participant 4.05
participants.locator: p. 7, Table 2 and Section 5.1; p. 8, Table 3; p. 20, SI 6

ai_tool.name_model: ChatGPT-3.5, zero-shot prompt adapted from Stevenson et al. with an added instruction to match mean human word count
ai_tool.how_used: Pre-generated ChatGPT AUT ideas were inserted among the example ideas shown before each trial (passive exposure). Participants ranked the six examples by creativity and then wrote their own idea; they did not interact with the model. In disclosed conditions AI examples carried a 'Source: A.I' label (p. 4, Section 3.2; p. 16, Figure 12).

task.description: Alternate Uses Task variant: one creative use per item for tire, pants, shoe, table, or bottle, after ranking six example ideas. Ideas fed forward as examples for later participants in the same condition-item response chain (chains reset every 20 trials; 7 chains per condition-item, 175 chains, 3,500 targeted responses).
task.duration: Study described to participants as taking 3-6 minutes; average 144.31 seconds per response (Table 2)

outcomes.name: Creativity (originality) of the submitted idea
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Predicted originality from the fine-tuned GPT-3 Davinci classifier of Organisciak et al. (r = 0.81 with human ratings overall; items chosen with r = 0.88-0.91). The paper calls it 'creativity' but it is the AUT originality score. Mixed model with crossed random intercepts for participant and response chain nested in item-condition; joint F test via emmeans. Evolution variant: likelihood-ratio test of a condition x trial-number interaction, chi2(4) = 6.52, p = 0.16 (p. 8).

contrasts.reported: conditionHiExposure_Undisclosed 0.050 (0.113), t = 0.443; joint test of condition F(4, 19.86) = 0.12, p = 0.97

outcomes.name: Global idea diversity (median pairwise distance among submitted ideas in a condition)
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Median pairwise SBERT cosine distance (x100) among 50 randomly sampled submitted ideas per condition-item, 50 Monte Carlo runs, ideas after the sixth trial of a chain. Robustness: mean pairwise distance (Table 11, p. 21) and mean distance to centroid (Table 13, p. 22), directionally similar. Arm levels with 95% CIs shown only in Figure 7 (p. 7). Higher = more diverse; no sign reversal needed.

contrasts.reported: Dif in Means 1.21; Adj P Value 0.001; Cliff's Delta 0.31 (text: delta = 0.31; p = 0.001)
contrasts.locator: p. 22, Table 12; p. 7, Section 5.2 and Figure 7

diversity_detail.metric: Median pairwise cosine distance between SBERT embeddings, scaled by 100
diversity_detail.embedding_model: SBERT (Sentence-BERT); the specific checkpoint is not named
diversity_detail.computed_over: All pairs within a random sample of 50 submitted ideas per condition-item combination, repeated for 50 Monte Carlo runs; only ideas submitted after the sixth trial of a response chain
diversity_detail.uncertainty: Two-tailed paired permutation tests (10,000 iterations), paired on Monte Carlo seed and item, with +1 adjustment and Holm-Bonferroni correction; Cliff's delta as effect size. No participant-level standard error.
diversity_detail.notes: Ideas within a response chain are not independent because each participant sees the previous participants' ideas. Figure 7 gives arm-level medians with 95% CIs only graphically.

outcomes.name: Evolution of idea diversity (slope of diversity on trial number in the response chain)
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Median pairwise SBERT cosine distance (x100) of the pool of ideas at each (item, condition, trial number) across chains, trials after the sixth; mixed model with item random intercepts, controlling for pool size (Nobs); contrasts are condition x trial-number interactions relative to Control. Robustness: mean pairwise distance and centroid distance, Table 17 columns 2-3 (similar). Control slope: beta = -0.39, t(349) = -2.23, 95% CI [-0.73, -0.05], p = 0.03.

contrasts.locator: p. 8, Section 5.3 and Figure 8; p. 25, Table 17
p. 8, Section 5.3 and Figure 8; p. 25, Table 17

diversity_detail.metric: Slope over trial number of the median pairwise cosine distance (x100) between SBERT embeddings
diversity_detail.embedding_model: SBERT (Sentence-BERT); the specific checkpoint is not named
diversity_detail.computed_over: All pairs within each pool of submitted ideas sharing item, condition, and trial number (pooled across response chains), trials 7 onward
diversity_detail.uncertainty: Linear mixed model on 362 pool-level observations with item random intercepts; t statistics and 95% CIs
diversity_detail.notes: This is a rate-of-change outcome, not a level.

outcomes.name: Local idea diversity (distance between a participant's idea and the examples that participant saw)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Median pairwise SBERT cosine distance (x100) between the submitted idea and the six example ideas shown (robustness: mean pairwise distance, centroid distance; Table 14 cols 2-3). Coded 'other' because it compares a person's idea with the stimuli (which mix AI ideas, seeds, and prior participants' ideas), not different people's outputs with each other. The model includes condition x moderator interactions (self-perceived creativity, AI-human creativity), so condition coefficients are at moderator values of zero. Reported only in the SI.

contrasts.reported: No main effect of condition, F(4, 19.95) = 0.09, p = 0.98. Table 14 col (1): LoExposure_Disclosed -1.467 (1.864); LoExposure_Undisclosed 0.272 (1.861); HiExposure_Disclosed 1.051 (1.864); HiExposure_Undisclosed -0.744 (1.866)

outcomes.name: AI adoption (maximum cosine similarity between the submitted idea and the AI examples seen)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Max SBERT cosine similarity (x100) to AI examples; robustness with mean and median similarity (Table 22). Defined only in the four AI conditions. The paper calls it a secondary outcome and does not interpret main effects because max similarity rises mechanically with more AI examples. Coded question 'none': it measures convergence toward AI examples, not creativity or diversity across people.

contrasts.reported: Main effect of condition F(3, 16.59) = 4.33, p = 0.02 (not interpreted). Self-perceived creativity x [High Exposure, Disclosed] beta = 0.11, t(2588) = 3.93, 95% CI = [0.06, 0.17], p = 0.0001. Exposure effect, undisclosed minus disclosed: high-creativity participants Delta = -1.69, d = -0.14, p = 0.59; low-creativity participants Delta = 7.77, d = 0.65, p = 0.03.
contrasts.locator: p. 9, Section 5.5.1 and Figure 9; p. 27, SI 10 and Table 19; p. 28, Table 22

sample_overlap.shares_participants_with: No overlap for the S1 experiment participants. S2 and the S1 seed examples reuse human AUT responses from the Organisciak et al. (2023) dataset; those people are not S1 participants.

company_involvement.description: None stated. Creative Mornings (a creative-professional community) distributed the study link (p. 4, Section 3.3). Acknowledgments name only academic colleagues.

eligibility.reason: S1 randomizes each participant to a within-person sequence in which the condition order (and item-condition mapping) is randomized (p. 5, Figure 2, Section 3.4.2); AI arms receive ChatGPT-generated example ideas (ideas_supplied) versus a control that sees only human examples. 844 unique participants analyzed (p. 7, Table 2). Originality is scored on each submitted idea by an automated classifier and diversity by SBERT distances. Caveats: AI help is passive exposure to example ideas, not interaction with a chatbot; per-arm participant counts are not reported and each person contributes to up to five arms (4.05 trials on average); outputs within response chains are not independent. S2 is ai_vs_human context only.

one_line_finding: Among 844 online volunteers (3,414 AUT ideas), seeing ChatGPT example ideas did not change classifier-scored originality (joint F(4, 19.86) = 0.12, p = 0.97; p. 8 and Table 18, p. 26), but high AI exposure raised global idea diversity over the human-examples control (Cliff's delta 0.31 disclosed, 0.26 undisclosed, adjusted p = 0.001; Table 12, p. 22).
open_questions: Text on p. 8 says only [Low Exposure, Undisclosed] had higher global diversity than Control (delta = 0.11, p = 0.001), but Table 12 (p. 22) gives Low Exposure Disclosed - Control = +0.47, delta 0.11, and Low Exposure Undisclosed - Control = -0.61, delta -0.06, adj p 0.0063; Figure 7 (p. 7) agrees with the table. The text appears to mislabel the arm.

The abstract says 'There were no main effects of disclosure', yet Table 12 reports disclosed > undisclosed global diversity at both exposure levels (0.41, adj p 0.0328; 1.08, adj p 0.001). The abstract claim may refer only to creativity.
Per-arm participant counts are not reported. Each person can appear in up to five arms (within-person design), so n_treatment and n_control for any contrast cannot be read from the paper.
3,414 responses are analyzed (Table 2, SI 3), but the creativity and local-diversity models report 3,271 observations (Tables 14, 18); the paper does not explain the difference.
Comparison type coded ai_vs_active because the control sees six human-written example ideas; a reviewer may prefer ai_vs_bau.
Whether passive exposure to AI example ideas (no interaction with the model) counts as 'generative-AI assistance' under criterion 1; coded met via the ideas_supplied role.
No participant-level standard error for diversity: global diversity uses Monte Carlo set samples with permutation tests; evolution uses 362 pool-level observations.
notes: Version read is arXiv v3 of 31 Jul 2025, the CI 2025 paper. Not extracted as outcomes: the word-length prompt experiment (Appendix A.2, Table 5, p. 13 and p. 17), which compares ChatGPT and human word counts and is not a creativity outcome; ranking accuracy and per-trial feedback (SI 5); moderator analyses of local diversity (Tables 15-16) beyond the main condition test; AI adoption tables by perceived AI creativity (Tables 20-21) and the task-difficulty correlation (rho = 0.8 vs 0.3, p. 9, Figure 10, based on five items). Participant counts per recruitment source sum to 844 (Table 3, p. 8).
